item.title: Eslabón Armado Breaks Down 5 Essential Songs From New Album ‘Nocturno’
item.description:
[Intro music plays]
Host: Welcome to our podcast, where we dive into the latest music news and trends. Today, we're excited to talk about the newest album from Eslabón Armado, a group that's been making waves in the regional Mexican music scene. Their ninth studio album, Nocturno, is out now, and it's a must-listen. Let's dive in.
[Soft music transition]
Host: Nocturno is a 16-track set that features the group's signature sound, with special guest appearances by Peso Pluma, Gabito Ballesteros, Clave Especial, and Calle 24. The album takes you on a journey through different styles, from requintos to charchetas, corridos, and even urban sounds.
[Clip of "Ojos de Diabla" plays in the background]
Host: According to singer-songwriter Pedro Tovar, most of the lyrics on the album are his, while the music was created by his bandmates Brian and Damián. Tovar gave his bandmates full freedom to experiment with the music, and the result is an album that's both authentic and innovative.
[Soft music transition]
Host: One thing that sets Eslabón Armado apart from other música tumbada groups is their commitment to avoiding explicit language in their lyrics. As Tovar says, "We've never disrespected women. Never." Instead, they focus on singing about love and everyday situations, making their music relatable and accessible to a wide audience.
[Clip of "Ella Baila Sola" plays in the background]
Host: You might remember Eslabón Armado's hit song "Ella Baila Sola," which they collaborated on with Peso Pluma. The song was a global hit, spending 19 weeks at number one on the Hot Latin Songs chart and even reaching number four on the Hot 100. Now, the two artists have teamed up again for a new track called "Amigos con Derechos," a corrido tumbado about a love triangle.
[Soft music transition]
Host: Eslabón Armado is gearing up for their Amor Nocturno Tour, a 28-date U.S. run that kicks off in July and wraps up in December. They'll also be performing at various festivals in Mexico, including the Festival Arre in Mexico City, where they'll share the stage with some of their collaborators.
[Outro music plays]
Host: That's all for today's episode. Nocturno is out now, and we highly recommend giving it a listen. With its unique blend of regional Mexican styles and urban sounds, it's an album that's sure to captivate music fans of all genres. Thanks for tuning in, and we'll catch you in the next episode!
